title: Denis Diderot's birth chart
metaDescription: Denis Diderot's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 12.1° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Virgo — Mercury, Saturn, Uranus and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 12.1° Libra: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. An air sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Virgo (24.2°), Venus in Leo (29.4°), Mars in Sagittarius (3.9°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Saturn a third of the circle apart from Neptune, 0.2° off exact. The scheme reads trines as water finding its level: effortless, and invisible to the person living it. Behind it, Mars square Jupiter at 0.3°, and Neptune trine Pluto at 0.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Venus opposes Jupiter while both square Mars. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Sun stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has three entries for this chart. The Sun in Libra at 12.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mercury in Virgo at 24.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Pisces at 4.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 earth, 2 fire, 1 air, 1 water; by modality, 6 mutable, 2 fixed, 1 cardinal. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Jupiter and Neptune were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.0° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
